# Spreadsheet

**Class:** `UltraCanvasSpreadsheet` · **Group:** [Navigation and data views](../Groups/Navigation-and-data-views.md) · **Header:** [`UltraCanvas/include/UltraCanvasSpreadsheet.h`](../../../UltraCanvas/include/UltraCanvasSpreadsheet.h) · `#include "UltraCanvasSpreadsheet.h"`

**Inherits:** [`UltraCanvasContainer`](UltraCanvasContainer.md) → [`UltraCanvasUIElement`](UltraCanvasUIElement.md) → `Element`

## What it is for

List **or table** — `UltraCanvasListView` is the multi-column, virtualised, model-driven one (`IListModel` + `ListColumnDef` + delegates; `SetShowHeader(true)` gives resizable columns, header tooltips and a sort indicator; sort and filter it with [`UltraCanvasListSortFilterProxy`](../../UltraCanvas/UltraCanvasListSortFilterProxy.md)); tree; multi-column tree ([`UltraCanvasColumnsTreeView`](../../UltraCanvas/UltraCanvasTreeViewExamples.md#columnar-layout-ultracanvascolumnstreeview): aligned Name / Type / Value columns with a header band, resizable boundaries and section-header rows); sheet

## Overview

A container, not a bare element: the cell / formula-bar editor is a real UltraCanvasTextInput child (caret, selection, clipboard, undo, IME) rather than a private buffer painted by hand.

## Creating it

Factory functions (the usual way - every element is held in a `std::shared_ptr`):

```cpp
CellTextMeasureFn MakeSpreadsheetTextMeasurer(IRenderContext* ctx);
std::shared_ptr<UltraCanvasSpreadsheet> CreateSpreadsheetElement( const std::string& id, float x, float y, float width, float height);
std::shared_ptr<UltraCanvasSpreadsheet> CreateSpreadsheetElement( const std::string& id, float width, float height);
```

Constructors:

```cpp
UltraCanvasSpreadsheet();
UltraCanvasSpreadsheet(const std::string& id, float x, float y, float width, float height);
UltraCanvasSpreadsheet(const UltraCanvasSpreadsheet&) = delete;
```

The first string argument is always the element's **identifier**, never its text (see [Core concepts](../Core-Concepts.md#identifiers)).

### enum `ValidationAnswer`

A rule is set on the sheet (GetActiveSheet()->SetValidation(range, rule)) or on one cell (GetCell(row, col)->SetValidation(rule)). A value typed into a cell is checked when the edit is committed: an entry that breaks the rule is answered as the rule's alertStyle says - Stop Retry (edit the entry again) or Cancel (the old value back) Warning Yes (keep it), No (edit it again) or Cancel Information OK (keep it) or Cancel A rule with showErrorAlert false keeps whatever is typed. Values set from code, pasted or filled are not checked; SpreadsheetSheet::ValidateCell checks any cell.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Accept` |  |
| `Retry` |  |
| `Cancel` |  |
